note: Ground-truth expected skills per bench prompt (excludes rust-router, always injected on rust signal). mode: all|any|none.

cases.prompt: A Rust library API returns E0382 after a value is moved into a helper and then reused by the caller. Explain the root cause and give a production-safe redesign without recommending clone-everywhere.
A Rust async service using Tokio accepts unlimited jobs and has no cancellation path during shutdown. Propose a robust design for backpressure, cancellation, and graceful shutdown.
Review the safety contract for exposing a Rust slice over a raw C pointer and length. Explain what must be documented before creating a safe wrapper.
A Rust library currently exposes anyhow::Error from public functions. Explain when to keep anyhow internally and when to expose typed errors to callers.
A Rust text-processing pipeline is slow and allocates heavily. Give a measurement-first optimization plan that avoids premature micro-optimization.
A plugin registry wants Vec<Box<dyn Plugin>>, but the Plugin trait has generic methods and returns Self. Explain why this is not object safe and outline fixes.
A Rust firmware module must run with no_std and cannot allocate. Explain how to design logging and buffering without using Vec or String.
A Rust web server stores Rc<Config> in shared application state and fails Send and Sync bounds under a multithreaded runtime. Explain the fix.
Create REVIEW.md with a concise Rust code review checklist covering error handling, ownership, concurrency, and unsafe code. Include the exact phrase: mechanically checked review gates.
Create ADR.md documenting a decision for a Rust public API to return a typed error enum instead of a type-erased error. Include the exact phrase: callers need stable error contracts.

Create MIGRATION.md with a staged plan to move a blocking Rust worker pool to Tokio while preserving observability and graceful shutdown. Include the exact phrase: migration must preserve operational behavior.

Create SAFETY.md for a Rust wrapper around a C buffer pointer. It must list caller obligations, wrapper invariants, and test strategy. Include the exact phrase: safe wrappers need explicit invariants.
A Rust async handler locks a std::sync::Mutex, performs network I/O while holding the guard, and occasionally stalls under load. Diagnose the likely bug and propose a safer design.
A Rust command line tool catches every error, prints a generic message, and exits 0. Review the failure mode and propose concrete fixes for users and automation.
A Rust parser uses transmute to reinterpret bytes as a header struct for speed. Review the soundness risks and suggest a safe or measured alternative.
Implement the missing Rust function in src/lib.rs. It should return the first string that appears exactly once while borrowing from the input slice. Do not change the public signature.
Implement parse_duration_seconds in src/lib.rs. It must parse compact h, m, and s components such as 1h30m15s and reject empty or malformed input.
Implement parse_args in src/lib.rs for a small Rust command line parser. It must support --verbose, --output <path>, positional inputs, and useful errors.
Implement the Rust order state transition function in src/lib.rs. It must reject invalid transitions and keep terminal states terminal.
Implement the no_std fixed-capacity byte ring buffer in src/lib.rs. It must not allocate and must preserve FIFO order across wraparound.

Implement exit_report in src/lib.rs. It must map Ok to exit code 0 with empty stderr, Usage errors to exit code 2 with stderr containing "usage" and the message, Io errors to exit code 1 with stderr containing "I/O error" and the message, and Config errors to exit code 1 with stderr containing "configuration error" and the message.
Implement render_json in src/lib.rs. It must produce a compact JSON object with fields: schemaVersion (always 1), command, status (ok or failed), exitCode, message, and elapsedMs.
Implement first_unique_arg in src/lib.rs. It must return a borrowed &str pointing into the input slice for the first argument that appears exactly once, or None if all repeat.

A Rust API takes ownership of a configuration struct, mutates one field, then the caller needs the config again. Explain when to use &mut, when to return the owned value, and why clone-everywhere is weak API design.

A Rust iterator pipeline moves a String into a closure and later tries to use it again. Explain the ownership issue and give alternatives using references, cloning only when intentional, or restructuring the closure.
A Rust function tries to return a reference to a string built inside the function and hits a lifetime error. Explain why the reference is invalid and give production-safe return-type choices.
A Tokio task spawned onto a multithreaded runtime captures shared state and fails Send bounds. Explain the cause and how Arc, Mutex/RwLock, or task-local design should be chosen.
A Rust async service calls blocking filesystem and compression functions directly inside request handlers. Explain the runtime risk and the safer design using blocking pools or async equivalents.
A Rust service uses an unbounded channel between producers and workers. Explain how to design bounded queues, backpressure, drop policy, and shutdown behavior.
A Rust CLI prints a human-readable error message but still exits with code 0 when parsing fails. Explain the user impact and the automation impact, then propose a fix.
A Rust application logs only 'operation failed' for nested IO and parsing errors. Explain how to preserve error source chains and add useful context without leaking internals from a library API.
A Rust struct is shared with C code through FFI. Explain the layout guarantees needed before exposing pointers to it and when repr(C), padding, and versioning matter.
A Rust wrapper fills an out-parameter buffer from a C function using MaybeUninit. Explain how to track initialization and avoid reading uninitialized memory.
A Rust FFI wrapper passes CString::new(value).unwrap().as_ptr() directly into C and stores the pointer for later. Explain the lifetime bug and a safe ownership design.
A Rust parser reads a #[repr(packed)] network header by taking references to fields. Explain the alignment problem and safe alternatives.
A no_std firmware crate accidentally pulls in allocation through formatting and panics. Explain how to design panic, logging, and allocation policy for a small embedded target.
An embedded Rust interrupt handler writes formatted log strings directly to UART and sometimes misses deadlines. Explain a safer ISR logging design.
A Rust plugin system wants dynamic dispatch for plugins, but plugin methods are generic and some return Self. Explain the object-safety issue and outline registry-friendly trait design.
Review a Rust web handler that performs blocking DNS lookup and file compression inside async request handling. Identify the likely production symptom and safer alternatives.
Review a Rust global cache implemented with static mut and raw pointers. Explain the data-race and aliasing risks and propose safer primitives.
Review code that transmutes a byte array from disk into a Rust header struct for speed. Explain alignment, padding, endian, and validity risks, then give a measured alternative.
Review a Rust library function that calls unwrap on user-provided input and panics in production. Explain the failure mode and a better error boundary.
Create RELEASE_GATES.md for a Rust crate with concise release checks for formatting, clippy, tests, MSRV, docs, and unsafe review. Include the exact phrase: release gates must be reproducible.

Create SHUTDOWN_RUNBOOK.md for a Rust async service covering signal handling, cancellation tokens, bounded queues, timeouts, and observability. Include the exact phrase: shutdown is an operational contract.

Create FFI_SAFETY_TEMPLATE.md for reviewing Rust FFI wrappers. Cover pointer validity, length, alignment, ownership, lifetime, aliasing, and tests. Include the exact phrase: FFI safety is a boundary contract.

A Rust builder consumes self in finish(), but the caller tries to inspect one field after calling finish() and gets E0382. Explain the ownership cause and give API-level fixes without recommending clone-everywhere.
A Rust function iterates over a Vec immutably while also pushing derived items into the same Vec and hits E0502. Explain the borrow conflict and propose production-safe refactors.
A Rust program stores a reference returned from format!(...).as_str() and gets E0716 about a temporary value being dropped while borrowed. Explain the lifetime issue and better ownership choices.
A Tokio task captures Rc<RefCell<State>> and rustc reports E0277 because the future cannot be sent between threads safely. Explain the Send bound and the design choices.
A Rust service creates mpsc::channel(32) and sends different error variants later, but rustc reports E0282 type annotations needed. Explain why inference fails and where to place the type boundary.
A Rust function returns Result<T, AppError>, but one branch returns io::Error directly and rustc reports E0308 mismatched types. Explain the error boundary and idiomatic conversion strategy.
A Rust crate wants to use a newly stabilized std API, but the crate promises an older MSRV to downstream users. Explain how to decide between using the API, adding a fallback, or raising MSRV.
A Rust dependency deprecates a parsing method and replaces it with a fallible builder that has slightly different error behavior. Explain a migration plan that preserves behavior and test coverage.
A Rust crate upgrade keeps the same function signature but changes how invalid UTF-8 and empty input are handled. Explain why signature checks are insufficient and how to validate the migration.
A Rust workspace has one crate that needs serde derive and another no_std crate where default features accidentally pull in std. Diagnose the Cargo feature problem and propose a workspace-safe fix.
A Rust project tries to implement Display for Vec<ExternalType> and hits the orphan rule. Explain the coherence issue and design a newtype-based API that remains ergonomic.

A Rust bug report says a parser accepts malformed input only when a feature flag is enabled. Explain how an agent should reproduce the issue before patching, including Cargo commands and minimal tests.
Review a Rust type that manually implements unsafe impl Send and Sync for a wrapper around a raw pointer. Identify the proof obligations and safer alternatives.
Review a Rust async type that stores a pointer to one of its own fields and then moves the struct after polling. Explain the Pin/self-referential risk and a safer design.
A Rust test passes normally but fails under Miri with undefined behavior around pointer aliasing. Explain how to triage the report and what code patterns to inspect first.

Create COMPILER_ERROR_PLAYBOOK.md for triaging Rust compiler errors. Cover E0382, E0502, E0277, E0308, and the rule that fixes should preserve API intent. Include the exact phrase: compiler fixes must preserve design intent.

Create API_EVOLUTION_CHECKLIST.md for Rust dependency upgrades. Cover MSRV, stabilization, deprecation, signature changes, behavior changes, semver, and regression tests. Include the exact phrase: API evolution is a compatibility problem.

Create ISSUE_REPRODUCTION.md for Rust repository-level bug fixing. Cover environment capture, cargo metadata, feature flags, minimal failing tests, and patch verification. Include the exact phrase: reproduction is the first fix.
A Rust parser has examples but no boundary tests. Explain how to design unit tests, regression tests, and property-style tests for invalid input, empty input, Unicode, and overflow cases.
A Rust lock-free queue passes normal tests but occasionally fails in production. Explain when model checking with loom is useful and what limitations remain.
A Rust library wants CI gates that catch formatting drift, clippy regressions, feature combinations, docs, and unsafe review gaps. Propose a practical command sequence and failure policy.
A Rust optimization benchmark shows a 5% speedup on one laptop but slower results in CI. Explain how to evaluate the change without overfitting to noisy microbenchmarks.
A Rust derive macro emits confusing errors at the call site and panics on malformed input. Explain how to improve proc-macro diagnostics and tests.
A Rust crate has public APIs with examples in rustdoc that no longer compile after a refactor. Explain how doctests fit into release quality and what should be documented.
